title: Risk of Post-Hemorrhoidectomy Bleeding in Lampang Hospital; A Retrospective Study
content: Introduction: Post hemorrhoidectomy bleeding (PHB) is an uncommon yet potentially serious complication of hemorrhoidectomy. The LigaSure system has been increasingly adopted as a substitute to conventional hemorrhoidectomy, yet comparative data on PHB and its risk factors remain limited. Methods: This retrospective cohort comprised 804 consecutive patients with symptomatic grade II–IV hemorrhoids who underwent hemorrhoidectomy at Lampang Hospital between January 2018 and April 2025. Of these, 610 patients underwent LigaSure hemorrhoidectomy (LH) and 194 underwent Ferguson hemorrhoidectomy (FH). Demographic data, comorbidities, medication use, operative characteristics, and postoperative bleeding events requiring hospitalization or reoperation were analyzed. Logistic regression was performed to identify independent predictors of PHB. Results: The overall incidence of PHB was 4.97%, with no significant difference between the LH and FH groups (5.41% vs. 3.61%, P value = 0.315). Multivariate analysis identified cirrhosis (OR 22.849, 95% CI 2.674–195.269), aspirin use (OR 4.643, 95% CI 1.180–18.266), hemorrhoid grade IV (OR 3.699, 95% CI 1.128–12.130), and urgent hemorrhoidectomy (OR 0.283, 95% CI 0.080–0.993) as independent predictors of PHB. Conclusions: In this large retrospective cohort, cirrhosis, aspirin use, and grade IV hemorrhoids were identified as independent predictors of post‑hemorrhoidectomy bleeding, whereas urgent operations were linked to a reduced risk. No significant difference in PHB incidence was observed between the LigaSure and Ferguson techniques.
